title: Exploring a shared registry approach with CFC International

sentences.text: We at RASopathies Network support families affected by HRAS-related disorders (Costello syndrome).
Costello syndrome and KRAS-related RASopathies share a mechanism in which a protein does too much, and HRAS and KRAS participate in the MAPK cell-signalling pathway.

The atlas infers CFC International’s KRAS community connection from CFC syndrome coverage; its broader symptom-similarity link with Costello syndrome is also inferred, with confidence 0.36, below 0.5.

sections.heading: What already exists that we could share

sentences.text: CFC International’s CITIZEN CFC Syndrome Registry offers a possible starting point, although its KRAS coverage is inferred by the atlas rather than explicitly named on the registry page.
PATRAS and the RASopathies Network contact registry are also listed, with their HRAS coverage inferred by the atlas.
We propose comparing registry designs before considering any shared approach.

sections.heading: What must be checked before we join forces

sentences.text: Please confirm whether thickened Achilles tendon and deep-set nails occur in KRAS-related RASopathies, and review bladder carcinoma and the additional symptom gaps flagged for registry adaptation.
Please check all listed differences, including the “12 more” symptoms not individually named in the adaptation notes, rather than treating missing records as proof of absence.

Before extending any study design, please check eligibility changes, Costello-specific family representation, and whether individual variants increase activity, impair protein function or cause loss of function.
This month, send CFC International one focused enquiry asking whether CITIZEN could include HRAS-related disorders (Costello syndrome), and what changes would be needed.
Which patient organisation specifically serves Costello syndrome, beyond the linked RASopathies Network?
Could we verify a Costello family-network contact through our network?
Which individual variants are activating, catalytically impaired—meaning their usual activity is reduced—or loss of function?
Could a variant-by-variant review of published functional evidence resolve this?
Dear CFC International team,
I am writing on behalf of our Costello syndrome community to explore a small collaboration.
Our conditions share evidence of overactive proteins.
Could your team consider whether CITIZEN could include HRAS-related disorders?
We would welcome an initial discussion of symptom coverage and eligibility before making commitments.
Thank you for considering this request.
[Your name], on behalf of RASopathies Network (RASopathiesNet USA / UK)
